c.tagline: Nomadic soul meets rising skyline beneath endless steppe sky.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmetered private cars hailed via app or roadside; negotiate or agree fare before riding, typically ~MNT 1,000-1,500/km.

emergency.note: Tourist Police hotline 1919 also available; English support limited outside major hospitals like Intermed and SOS Medica.

hood_desc: The historic and commercial core around Chinggis Khaan (Sukhbaatar) Square, walking distance to museums, government buildings, restaurants and nightlife; best for first-time visitors and business travelers.
A long commercial corridor lined with shops, banks, and budget lodging with strong transit links; suits budget travelers and those arriving by train who want easy access across the city.
The area around Gandan Monastery offering an authentic, less touristy slice of local life with morning prayer atmosphere; suits culture seekers wanting an alternative to the city center.
A southern district near the airport road with modern towers, embassies, and business hotels; suits business travelers and those with early flights.
An upscale, leafy area near Zaisan Hill Memorial and the Bogd Khan mountain foothills with cleaner air and expat-friendly cafes; suits families and longer stays.
lodging: The Corporate Hotel and Convention Centre

water.note: Aging infrastructure means tap water often falls short of safe standards; drink bottled, boiled, or filtered water.

transit.pay: Fares are paid with the U Money smart card (MNT 3,600 to purchase, top up at kiosks/shops), tapped on boarding; cash is largely phased out on buses. Transfers within 30 minutes on another bus are free.
transit.hours: Approx. 6:00am-11:00pm; frequency drops significantly late evening, taxis/apps recommended at night
transit.note: Roughly 1,200 buses across ~79 routes; the UB Smart Bus app provides English-language route tracking.

tip.r: Not traditionally expected; rounding up or 5-10% at higher-end restaurants is appreciated but not required.
